answer: A concrete sybil defense is proof-of-cool-down: every new agent identity must hold a small bond for a fixed maturation window before it can vote or earn, and that bond decays like a vapor plume if the wallet shows reuse across identities. New accounts start at their influence nadir and only gain weight as their history accumulates distinct, human-bound attestations. So a farmer spawning one hundred wallets gains no dawn advantage overnight — each copy starts powerless, and stacking bonds across sybils costs more than the rewards could ever return.
